cf.title: extension_control_path: ignore empty elements and deduplicate directories

input.subject: extension_control_path: ignore empty elements and deduplicate directories

verdict_reasoning: The goal is a valid bug fix and three reviewers reproduced the defect. The open point is the behaviour for invalid elements: v4 raises errors on every lookup, while message #9 reports an off-list committer preference for skipping them (standards-compat-1). The thread also has not chosen one rule for 18, 19 and master (standards-compat-2). Both are fixable, but the list must agree on them before code review is useful.

brief.title: extension_control_path: handle empty and relative path elements consistently
brief.problem: An empty element in extension_control_path, as in '$system:', expands to the literal directory /extension, which is then searched and can supply extensions. The views also list extensions from relative elements that CREATE EXTENSION later rejects. This affects anyone who sets the parameter with a stray separator or a relative path.
brief.proposed_design: v4-0001 makes get_extension_control_directories() reject empty elements with the existing "zero-length component" error, and v4-0002 moves the absolute-path check there too. extension_file_exists(), used for the unknown-language hint, skips such elements instead, so the original CREATE FUNCTION or DO error is kept. The v1 directory deduplication patch was dropped in v3.
user_visible_surface: extension_control_path: a nonempty value with an empty element now raises "zero-length component in parameter" on every lookup; an entirely empty value still means $system.
extension_control_path: a relative element now makes pg_available_extensions, pg_available_extension_versions and CREATE EXTENSION fail with "is not an absolute path".
CREATE FUNCTION and DO with an unknown language keep the "language does not exist" error and skip invalid elements when building the hint.
config.sgml adds the sentence "Empty elements within a nonempty value are not allowed."
author_claims: Searching /extension because of a trailing colon is unintended and easy to trigger by mistake.
The views and CREATE EXTENSION have disagreed on empty and relative elements since the parameter was added in 18.
The author thinks the error-raising change does not need a back-patch.
Deduplicating directories was low value but harmless, for example with extension directories on network storage.
brief.thread_state: Three reviewers took part, and two of them objected to deduplication, so the author dropped it. In the last message Matheus reports that Peter, off list, prefers silently ignoring invalid elements, which conflicts with v4 raising errors, and no new version follows.
unclear: The thread does not say whether v4 will switch back to silently skipping elements, as the off-list Peter view suggests, or keep the errors.
It does not say whether relative elements would also be skipped silently under that approach.
The back-patch scope to 18 and 19 is not decided.
The CommitFest entry title still mentions deduplication, which the thread dropped.
No posted version has tests that show DEBUG3 logging was removed, though the author said raising errors would let him remove it.

objections.title: Rejecting empty and relative elements breaks settings that work today
objections.failure_scenario: An admin on 18 has extension_control_path = '$system:' or '$system:$system/foo' in postgresql.conf, and extensions install fine. After upgrading, the server starts without complaint, but every pg_available_extensions query and every CREATE EXTENSION fails with "zero-length component" or "is not an absolute path". Any role running the views or a tool that lists extensions finds out first, not the admin.
objections.argument: Message #5 and message #7 show that a trailing separator and a trailing relative element both work on 18 and become errors with v4 on every lookup. The check runs at use time, so SET and ALTER SYSTEM accept the value and the failure appears later, possibly for unprivileged roles. Message #9 says nonexistent directories are skipped today and reports that the off-list committer view is to skip invalid elements the same way. v4 still raises errors, so it departs from the project's existing handling of path elements that do not apply.
objections.author_must_show: Why should a value that works on 18 fail on every extension lookup after upgrade, when skipping it matches how nonexistent directories are already treated?

critic.reasoning: Messages #5 and #7 confirm that '$system:' and '$system:$system/foo' work on 18 and fail on every lookup with v4. Message #9 reports a committer preference for skipping, and no later version answers it. Raising at use time does match dynamic_library_path, so the consistency point is weaker than stated.

objections.title: Back-branch behaviour left open gives one GUC different meanings by version
objections.failure_scenario: An operator manages 18, 19 and 20 servers from one configuration template that contains '$system:'. If master raises errors while 18 and 19 skip the element or keep searching /extension, the same template gives three different results. The operator finds out when extension listing fails on only the newest cluster.
objections.argument: In message #6 the author proposes erroring on master and perhaps skipping silently on released branches. Message #7 objects that the same setting should not behave differently across versions of a parameter that was only added in 18. The thread does not settle this, and v4 does not say which behaviour 18 and 19 get. A committer would likely ask for one rule for all branches before committing anything.
objections.author_must_show: Which single behaviour for empty and relative elements will 18, 19 and 20 share, and will v4 change to match it?

critic.reasoning: The author suggests errors on master and perhaps skipping on released branches in message #6. Message #7 asks for one rule on all branches, and the thread ends without a decision or a matching patch version.

refuted.title: Two validation modes in one helper, against the off-list committer preference
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a new reader of extension_control_path, such as a view or a lookup for the directory option discussed in the linked thread. It calls get_extension_control_directories() with skip_invalid_path = false, and a stray separator in postgresql.conf now replaces that code path's own error. Nothing fails until a user with that setting hits it.
refuted.argument: v4 gives one helper two behaviours: it raises an error for CREATE EXTENSION and the views, and skips the element for the unknown-language hint. Every future caller must choose a mode correctly, and message #5 shows the wrong choice already happened once. Message #9 reports a committer view that invalid elements should be ignored silently, like nonexistent directories are today. That design would remove the flag and the split, and v4 has not been reconciled with it.
refuted.author_must_show: If invalid elements are skipped everywhere, as message #9 suggests, what does raising errors still buy that justifies a two-mode helper?

critic.reasoning: A future lookup that raises on an invalid setting is what v4 intends, and the error is visible. Message #5 found a missing case in v2, before the flag existed, and the conflict with message #9 is covered by standards-compat-1.

refuted.title: Release branches may behave differently for one setting
refuted.failure_scenario: An administrator keeps '$system:' in postgresql.conf, which works on 18 and 19, and upgrades to 20. After the upgrade, pg_available_extensions and CREATE EXTENSION fail for every role. The administrator finds out on the first extension lookup, not at server start.
refuted.argument: The author proposes errors on master only, and skipping on back branches if a back-patch is done at all (message #6). Message #7 objects that the same value would then behave differently by version, for a parameter added in 18. Message #9 points toward silent skipping on all branches, and the thread leaves this open. The project would maintain and document two behaviours for a young parameter.
refuted.author_must_show: Which single behaviour for empty and relative elements will apply on 18, 19 and 20, and how is it back-patched?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2 for the branch question. Its failure scenario repeats the upgrade breakage in standards-compat-1.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: v4-0002 makes find_in_paths() static, which matters if any of this is back-patched.

touch_points.label: new GUC
touch_points.reason: No new GUC, but v4 changes which values of extension_control_path are usable and documents the restriction in config.sgml.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: A '$system:' setting carried into a new cluster would make CREATE EXTENSION fail during restore.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: The patch stops an unintended search of /extension; the v1 DEBUG3 message that showed paths to any role was dropped.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The defect exists in 18 and 19, and the thread has not decided what those branches get.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: get_extension_control_directories() gains a skip_invalid_path mode that each caller must choose.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Will the next version skip invalid elements silently, as message #9 reports, or keep the v4 errors, and why?
If empty elements are skipped, are relative elements skipped too, or do they still raise "is not an absolute path"?
Which single behaviour for empty and relative elements will 18, 19 and master share?
If errors are kept, why not reject the value in a check hook at SET time instead of on every lookup?
Should the CommitFest entry title drop "deduplicate directories", since the thread dropped that patch?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows extension.c and the extension_control_path code from 18. Message #9 relays a committer view from off list, but no committer has posted in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a behaviour change to a GUC added in 18: either a new error on settings that work today, or a silent skip that stays the rule on all branches.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted four versions in about a week and dropped the deduplication patch after review. No version follows message #9 yet.

priority.reason: The fix is two small patches in extension.c for a mistake that only affects clusters with a stray separator or a relative element. The error-or-skip choice and the branch scope must be settled before a committer can act.

provisional_note: The code was not read. Whether every caller of get_extension_control_directories() passes the right skip_invalid_path value, and whether the canonicalization changes in v4-0002 alter the reported locations, could not be checked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Configurable location for extension .control files
precedents_retrieved.summary: The thread started with a request to make the directory that holds extension .control files configurable, so isolated package layouts such as NixOS can install extensions outside SHAREDIR/extension. A 2015 patch added an extension_directory setting that superusers can change at runtime, mainly so extension authors can test their .control files in a local cluster.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected in 2013 that the path should not be adjustable at runtime because of security concerns. In review, Heikki Linnakangas said tests also need dynamic_library_path changed, and other share data such as timezone and tsearch files is not covered. He proposed that pgxs build a temporary installation so "make check" works for extensions, and the entry was returned with feedback in that direction.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: In summary, the goal is to make "make check" to work for extensions, and the way to do that is to teach pgxs to create a temporary installation.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fast path for empty relids in check_outerjoin_delay()
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an early return in check_outerjoin_delay() when the given relids are empty, using the same fast path as when the query has no special joins. The stated aim was readability, with no expected performance gain.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut argued that extra fast paths with no performance benefit make the code harder to read and maintain. Tom Lane added that empty relids reach check_outerjoin_delay() only from check_equivalence_delay, so the test belongs there if anywhere, and he saw no gain in speed or readability. He suggested a larger refactoring of check_outerjoin_delay and SpecialJoinInfo, and closed the entry when no follow-on patch arrived by the end of the January commitfest.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Anyway, I concur with Peter that the patch you've presented should
probably be rejected: I doubt it's a win performance-wise and I don't
see that it adds anything to readability either.

precedents_retrieved.title: Strip Windows newlines from extension script files manually.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Strip Windows newlines from extension script files manually.
Reverted commit(s): Read extension script files in text not binary mode.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Revert commit 924e03917 in favor of adding code to convert \r\n to \n
explicitly, on Windows only.  The idea of letting text mode do the
work fails for a couple of reasons:

* Per Microsoft documentation, text mode also causes control-Z to be
interpreted as end-of-file.  While it may be unlikely that extension
scripts contain control-Z, we've historically allowed it, and breaking
the case doesn't seem wise.

* Apparently, on some Windows configurations, "r" mode is interpreted
as binary not text mode.  We could force it with "rt" but that would
be inconsistent with our code elsewhere, and it would still require
Windows-specific coding.

Thanks to Alexander Lakhin for investigation.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix search_path for maintenance commands
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch sets search_path to "pg_catalog, pg_temp" while ANALYZE, CLUSTER, REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW, REINDEX, VACUUM and CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW run as the table owner. This makes the commands behave the same for every caller and keeps a role with the MAINTAIN privilege from using search_path to gain the table owner's privileges.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Jeff Davis withdrew the patch after a reviewer reported that it no longer applied to HEAD, saying it was not yet clear this was the right change. He had already noted that it forces search_path in maintenance commands but not in other contexts, and that his broader proposals to fix search_path for functions got little agreement. Earlier concerns about breaking functions that depend on search_path were raised in messages not shown. Nathan Bossart supported committing it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I am withdrawing this patch from the CF until it's more clear that this is what we really want to do.

precedents_retrieved.title: Permute underscore separated components of columns before fuzzy matching
precedents_retrieved.summary: Extend the fuzzy column-name matching behind the "Perhaps you meant" hint so that it also checks permutations of up to three underscore-separated words. A swap of two words costs the same as one mistyped character, and the permutation is skipped when the typed name has more than six underscores.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the patch adds opaque, almost undocumented code to the matching function, and he doubted that many users want this behavior. He also noted that adjacent underscores and leading or trailing underscores are not handled well. The visible messages show no reply from the author after this review, and the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
However, we *do*
need to be concerned about its maintainability, and I think the patch
falls down badly there: it adds a chunk of very opaque and essentially
undocumented code, that people will need to reverse-engineer anytime
they are studying this function.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow excluding pg_temp or pg_catalog from search_path.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds special search_path entries "!pg_temp" and "!pg_catalog" that stop Postgres from searching pg_temp or pg_catalog implicitly, as a safety option for functions. It also warns when a user creates a schema with one of these special names, such as "$user".
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author doubted the feature's value without his separate SEARCH clause proposal, which did not gain support, because users would have to type "!pg_temp" by hand and pg_temp is already ignored for function and operator lookup. The reviewer agreed it was not worth adding without that main use case, and the author withdrew the entry. Earlier review comments also noted that the names need quoting and that "!pg_temp" is ignored when pg_temp is listed explicitly.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I thought it sounded generally useful, but if we're not going to proceed
with the primary use-case for this feature, then perhaps it's not worth
going through this particular one-way door at this time.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add checks on search_path for IMMUTABLE and SECURITY DEFINER functions
precedents_retrieved.summary: Greg Stark proposed checks at function creation that warn or error when an IMMUTABLE or SECURITY DEFINER function has no search_path set, so that pg_restore failures and index corruption caused by search_path dependence are avoided. A later version instead filled in search_path in proconfig for the user, and he also floated a LEXICAL option modelled on SQL-standard function bodies.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stayed a work in progress: it failed the regression tests, and the author raised open issues himself, namely cache flushes from a per-function search_path and the loss of inlining for functions with proconfig set. Andres Freund noted in October that it did not pass tests and asked whether the author planned further work and whether the entry wanted review. No reply from the author is shown.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This currently obviously doesn't pass tests - are you planning to work on this
further?  As is I'm not really clear what the CF entry is for.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert exporting of internal GUC variable "data_directory".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert exporting of internal GUC variable "data_directory".
Reverted commit(s): Use GUC lexer for recovery.conf parsing.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This undoes a poorly-thought-out choice in commit 970a18687f9b3058, namely
to export guc.c's internal variable data_directory.  The authoritative
variable so far as C code is concerned is DataDir; there is no reason for
anything except specific bits of GUC code to look at the GUC variable.

After yesterday's commits fixing the fsync-on-restart patch, the only
remaining misuse of data_directory was in AlterSystemSetConfigFile(),
which would be much better off just using a relative path anyhow: it's
less code and it doesn't break if the DBA moves the data directory of a
running system, which is a case we've taken some pains over in the past.

This is mostly cosmetic, so no need for a back-patch (and I'd be hesitant
to remove a global variable in stable branches anyway).

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_regress.c: Fix "make check" on Mac OS X: Pass DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_regress pass DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH explicitly to the shell commands it runs on macOS, because System Integrity Protection removes that variable and "make check" then cannot load libpq from the temporary install. It adds a global extra_envvars string that is empty elsewhere and holds "DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=..." on macOS.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch fixes only pg_regress, but other test suites hit the same problem, so a fix would need changes potentially everywhere system() is called. Tom Lane said a patch that does not handle all test cases from "make check-world" would not get much support. David Zhang's tests showed isolation and TAP tests still fail, and the visible messages contain no updated patch from the author.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This addresses only pg_regress.  What about all the other test suites?
Per the previous discussions, you'd need to patch up other places in a
similar way, potentially everywhere system() is called.

precedents_retrieved.title: makes pgbench functions available on server side - Common Library Extraction (patch 1 - refactoring only) & Server Extension (patch 2 adds extension)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patches move pgbench's random distribution generators, permutation and 64-bit hash routines from src/bin/pgbench/pgbench.c into src/common, and pgbench calls the shared copies. A second patch adds a contrib/pgbench extension that exposes these routines as SQL functions in schema pgbench, so the same workloads can run in pgbench and on the server.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Only the opening message is shown, with no replies, and the entry was withdrawn about seven weeks later.

precedents_retrieved.summary:

Reverted commit(s): Add TAP test to automate the equivalent of check_guc
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit b0a55f4, to remove for now the TAP test that did the
equivalent of check_guc.  The test has been using pg_config --sharedir
to find the location of postgresql.conf.sample.  While the buildfarm and
normal build environments rather liked that, this proves to be an issue
for Debian where pg_config is patched to not be relocatable, causing the
test to fail.

Rather than relying on pg_config, we'd better find the sample file based
on its location from the source directory.  However, this is also an
issue as a TAP test only offers the build directory as of TESTDIR in the
environment context, so this would fail with VPATH builds.  Perhaps the
source path could be provided additionally when running the TAP tests.
Or perhaps we may be able to get away by just switching to a SQL
approach, by using PG_ABS_SRCDIR but this is going to require some extra
loops to get the sample file from the correct path in src/backend/.  In
any case, this needs more thoughts, so just revert the test case until
something better is done about this relocation problem.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P2] made the extension control directory configurable, and [P14] has no recorded reason, so neither reason applies to path validation. Message #7 points to an earlier documentation thread with the same '$system/foo' inconsistency; that thread asked about a check hook and did not reject the idea. Message #9 reports an off-list committer preference for silently skipping invalid elements, which v4 has not yet followed.
Other parts of the contract look consistent. v4 reuses the existing dynamic_library_path error message, keeps '' meaning $system, keeps the unknown-language error, and dropped deduplication.

The patch changes only how extension.c parses a superuser-only GUC. It adds no on-disk, WAL, catalog, protocol or replication state. Two side points belong to other angles: a '$system:' setting carried into a v20 cluster could fail CREATE EXTENSION during restore, and back-patching would need find_in_paths() to stay non-static.

No security objection. The only exposure in the thread, the DEBUG3 message that showed the share path to any role (message #3), was dropped from v4. The error texts name the parameter but not its value, and only superusers can set extension_control_path.
The proposal is a small, contained bugfix in extension.c with no hot-path cost. The objections above concern only which behaviour to keep and how many modes the code must carry.

This is a bug fix to an existing parameter. No existing feature, extension or tool can stop extension_control_path from turning an empty element into /extension, so the need is not already met. The dropped deduplication patch would have been the only duplication of existing behaviour, since the views already deduplicate by extension name.

This is a bug fix, so demand is shown by the defect itself: a trailing colon makes the server search /extension, and the views disagree with CREATE EXTENSION on relative elements. Prashant (message #2), Surya (message #3) and Matheus (message #5) reproduced both. The dedup patch, the only part with weak demand, was dropped in message #6. Error versus silent skip is a design and compatibility question for other angles.
